stimulus: A printmaker is producing an edition of $p$ linocut prints. She pays a one-time fee of $\$45$ to have the block cut and $\$3$ for the paper and ink for each print. She sells each print for $\$12$. She wants her total cost to be at most $\$60$ less than her total revenue from selling all $p$ prints.
explanation: Total cost is the fee plus the paper and ink: $45 + 3p$. Total revenue is $12p$. "$\$60$ less than" the revenue means you start with the revenue and subtract 60, so you get $12p - 60$. "At most" means $\le$. Together that gives $45 + 3p \le 12p - 60$.

A.why: You wrote "$\$60$ less than the revenue" as $60 - 12p$. "$k$ less than $X$" means $X - k$, so the revenue comes first: $12p - 60$.

B.why: You used $\ge$ for "at most." "At most" sets a ceiling on the cost, so the sign must be $\le$.

D.why: You left out the one-time $\$45$ fee for cutting the block. The total cost includes that fee as well as $3p$.

stimulus: An ornithologist surveying two neighboring marsh plots finds that the numbers of active heron nests in the plots are consecutive odd integers. Let $n$ be the smaller of the two counts. Three times the larger count is no more than 14 less than five times the smaller count.
explanation: Consecutive odd integers differ by 2, so the larger count is $n + 2$, and three times it is $3(n + 2)$. "14 less than five times the smaller count" is $5n - 14$. "No more than" means $\le$. The inequality is $3(n + 2) \le 5n - 14$.

A.why: You used $n + 1$ for the next count. That is the next integer, which is even when $n$ is odd. The next odd integer is $n + 2$.

C.why: You wrote "14 less than $5n$" as $14 - 5n$. "$k$ less than $X$" means $X - k$, so it should be $5n - 14$.

D.why: You used $\ge$ for "no more than." "No more than" is an upper limit, so it means $\le$.

stimulus: A musicologist is cataloging $r$ field recordings of work songs. Each recording takes 45 minutes to transcribe and another 15 minutes to annotate. The project also needs a single 150-minute session to set up the equipment. The grant that funds the project requires a minimum of 1,200 minutes of logged work, counting the setup session.
explanation: Each recording takes $45 + 15 = 60$ minutes, so $r$ recordings take $60r$ minutes. Adding the setup session gives $60r + 150$ minutes. "A minimum of" means the total must be 1,200 or more, so the inequality is $60r + 150 \ge 1{,}200$.

A.why: You treated 1,200 minutes as a maximum. The grant names a minimum, so the total must be $\ge 1{,}200$.

B.why: You counted only the 45 minutes of transcription. Each recording also needs 15 minutes of annotation, so it takes 60 minutes in total.

C.why: You subtracted the setup time. The setup session is extra logged work, so you add it to the total.

stimulus: A materials scientist cuts rectangular strips of a polymer film for tensile testing. Each strip has width $w$ centimeters, and its length is 4 centimeters more than its width. The testing protocol requires the perimeter of each strip to be at least 3 times the strip's length.
explanation: The length is $w + 4$, so the perimeter is $2w + 2(w + 4) = 4w + 8$. Three times the length is $3(w + 4) = 3w + 12$. "At least" means $\ge$, so the inequality is $4w + 8 \ge 3w + 12$.

A.why: You used $\le$, which treats 3 times the length as a maximum. "At least" means the perimeter must be greater than or equal to it, so the sign is $\ge$.

C.why: You used $w + (w + 4) = 2w + 4$. That is only half the perimeter. A rectangle has two widths and two lengths, so the perimeter is $4w + 8$.

D.why: You multiplied the width by 3 instead of the length. The protocol compares the perimeter with 3 times the length, which is $3(w + 4) = 3w + 12$.
